title: White Swan Yeast Cakes - Ferment, Sponge and Dough Method
description: A cake made with yeast, liquid, and lard.
steps: Preparation of Ferment: Put a pint of water at a temperature of about 90° F. into a bowl, drop the dry yeast cake into it and soak for half an hour, then stir in enough flour to make a thin batter, add one tablespoon sugar, and beat with a dover beater until well mixed and full of bubbles. Stand in a temperature of 70° to 80° F. until light, which will take from four to five hours.

Preparation of Sponge: When the ferment is ready, put the rest of the sugar, salt and lard into a kneading-pan, bring the rest of the liquid to 90° F. and add it to the ingredients in the pan. Add enough strong flour to make a batter that will beat without spattering; add the ferment and beat until it looks smooth and elastic. This will probably take 15 or 20 minutes. Cover closely, and keep at a temperature of 70° F., until light and spongy. This will take from 9 to 10 hours.

Preparation of Dough: When the sponge is ready stir in strong flour until too stiff to use the spoon, then mix in more with a stiff-bladed knife or the hand, until the dough no longer sticks to the fingers. Turn the dough out on the moulding-board to knead, leaving the pan quite clean. The dough should knead without flour being put on the board or hands; if it proves sticky return it to the pan and mix in more flour. Knead lightly until the mass is elastic and velvety, the surface covered with a film of tiny bubbles, and a cut with a sharp knife shows the inside full of fine even bubbles, and free from lumps or unmixed portions. Grease the kneading-pan lightly with lard, warm both pan and cover if they are cold, put in the dough, cover closely, and keep at a temperature of 80° F. until rather more than doubled in volume, or until a gentle slap with the tips of the fingers causes it to fall in. This will take from 2 to 3 hours.
Knead lightly in the pan for a minute to get rid of the larger bubbles and return to rise a second time until double in volume. This will take from 1 to 2 hours.

Divide into loaves that will half fill the bread tins. Knead each piece only enough to get rid of large bubbles and smooth the surface, and put it into a greased tin. Keep at a temperature of 70° to 80° F. until doubled in volume, when they should have a bold, nicely-rounded appearance.
Bake an hour in an oven about 350° F. When done, the loaves should give a hollow sound when tapped on the bottom.
When baked remove at once from the pan, and stand on edge or across the top of the pans, that the air may get to all parts and cool it quickly.

title: Buchty (Buchta Buns)
description: A bread preparation made with egg yolks, yeast, and filling or preserves or curd.

ingredients.name: filling: preserves, curd, or poppy seed

steps: Rub one-eighth kilogram of butter on a baking sheet until foamy
Season with salt
Add 6 decagrams sugar, lemon zest, 4 egg yolks, and 2 whole eggs, and rub together
Add one kilogram of flour and mix with 3 decagrams of diluted yeast
Beat the dough until it no longer sticks to hands
Let it rise
Roll out and flatten pieces
Fill with preserves, curd, or poppy seed
Place on greased sheet
Oil them
Let rise for a quarter hour
Bake in oven
When baked, sprinkle with sugar and vanilla

description: Prepared with cream, ice, and sour milk.

ingredients.name: 15 grams (1 lot) of finely beaten ice

steps: Add finely beaten ice to 17 liters of cream

When the sour milk is lukewarm, let it cool

description: Prepared with curd.

title: Butter Tarts
description: A pastry dish made with butter, egg yolks, and filling.

ingredients.name: optional: apples, peaches, plums, strawberries, cherries or other suitable fruit

steps: Sift one quart of dry flour onto a work surface
Crumble three-quarters pound of fresh butter into it finely
Mix it, gather into a mound, make a well in the center
Put six egg yolks, half a cup of cold water, one tablespoon of fine sugar, and a pinch of salt into the well
Mix with a knife, then knead with hands
Roll out the dough and fold it, roll it out again and fold again
Dust a clean cloth with flour, wrap the dough in it, and let it rest for half an hour in a cold place or on ice
Roll out the dough again and cut into square or round pieces
Fill with fine filling and form tarts according to the previous recipe
Place on a baking sheet lined with buttered paper
Alternatively, line a baking dish with dough rolled to about half a finger thickness and place quartered apples, halved fresh peaches, plums, strawberries, cherries or other suitable fruit on top
Sprinkle with sugar to taste and bake until golden

title: Bába (Babka)
description: Prepared with rolls, almonds, and raisins.

ingredients.name: three and three-quarters deciliters good sweet sour cream

steps: Cut fourteen hard rolls in half, then into small flat cakes.
Scald two handfuls almonds, peel, and chop coarsely; wash raisins in cold water, let dry, and pick over.
Mix six dekagrams crushed sugar with cinnamon; peel and slice six larger apples or pears and mix everything together.
Grease a mold with butter and sprinkle with grated bread.
Place mixture in mold, pour over three and three-quarters deciliters good sweet sour cream mixed with three eggs and six dekagrams butter.
Top with pieces of butter and bake in the oven.
If fresh fruit is unavailable, cottage cheese or dried plums may be used instead of apples or pears.

title: Bábovka (Crown Cake)
description: A cake made with yeast, lard, and raisins.
steps: The evening before, make a starter from one yeast cake, which should be nicely soured by morning
Next day take half pound fresh butter, half pound good lard, half pound sugar, mix everything well together
Beat in 6 yolks one at a time with constant stirring and 2 whole eggs
Add two small cups milk
Pour in the yeast starter, mix well and add flour until it is like thick porridge
Pepper quarter pound or more raisins, mix them into the batter and let it rise
Grease the form and sprinkle with breadcrumbs
Put the batter into it, let it rise again and bake
When baked, sprinkle it well with ground sugar
Do not forget salt, as that is understood by itself

title: Báhovka (Babovka Cake)
description: A cake made with egg yolks, yeast, and sour cream.
steps: Rub 9 decagrams of rendered butter until foamy
Add 9 decagrams of fresh butter
Add 10 egg yolks, each well mixed
Add 3 tablespoons yeast, 24 decagrams flour, 5 tablespoons good sour cream, a little vanilla and salt
Bake the babovka

title: Bílá cibulová omáčka (White Onion Sauce)
description: A sauce made with onion, beef broth, and butter.
steps: Chop the onion into fine pieces
Stew it in butter until soft and white
Add a tablespoon of flour and mix well
Pour beef broth over it and let it cook for about half an hour
If you want the sauce sour, add a little vinegar before cooking

title: Bílá kmínová omáčka (White Caraway Sauce)
description: A sauce made with caraway, meat, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: a quarter liter of clear meat broth

steps: Make a light roux from two tablespoons of flour and butter
Boil it with a quarter liter of clear meat broth
Add one tablespoon of crushed caraway
Season with salt
Mix in two beaten egg yolks and butter
